reviewed_by: Codex scoped process-worker experiment review; independent causal validation by validate_cpu_scaling
reason: Explicitly injected CPU worker prototype keeps one Core coordinator and isolates pure PDF layout. Selected cases prove process identity, coordinator callbacks, FIFO/count/byte admission, queued/running cancellation, ordinary job errors, worker replacement without replay, startup/loop ownership, shutdown cleanup, real report PDF equivalence/cache/authorization/retry/durable state, preserved report contracts and harness bookkeeping. Synthetic LAN stress and soak run separately on only these integration boundaries. User added live Butler host-load capability: include fresh authenticated project/global/managed reads, shared off-loop sampling, discovery/authorization and existing admission, plus help/catalog and product source-digest/Chroma sync gates. UI metadata has one focused catalog test. A branch-scoped temporary CI builder regenerates the model-backed help index because local model egress is denied; it runs no suites and will be removed after the generated resource is fetched.
exclusions: No full suites. The CPU prototype is constructor-injected and leaves the shipped default unchanged. Butler adds read-only live host-capacity discovery and one focused frontend catalog metadata case; no new controls, geometry, browser-origin or authentication behavior. Native/Playwright suites are outside these boundaries. No production data, live providers or security tools. Local Python3.12; focused CI coverage selects3.11/3.12/3.13 for spawned-process lifecycle. Frozen/native packaging, Windows/macOS execution and whole-Core horizontal scaling remain outside the prototype.
